newsitem.title: MOROCCO: FOCUS - Morocco's bullish bourse to stagnate soon.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Morocco's bullish bourse to stagnate soon.

text.p: Morocco's bourse, which showed an exceptional market capitalisation of 100 billion dirhams ($10.6 billion) in the first quarter of 1997, is expected to stagnate soon, Moroccan market analysts said.

In a quarterly report sent to Reuters on Tuesday, Casablanca Finance Intermediation (CFI) said: "The 1997 first quarter ended with a record 37 percent market performance and a total market capitalisation of 100 billion dirhams."
Traded volumes were higher than those registered in the first quarter of 1996, CFI report said.
"The impact of 1996 results and the 2.8 billion dirhams collected by mutual funds were the main factors behind the Casablanca bourse performances earlier this year" the report said.
But it is realistic to say "a stagnation or maybe a slight drop of the overall market activity will take place soon," CFI said but the report gave no details on the stagnation period duration.

Most of the stocks, including Morocco's largest conglomerates ONA Group and Societe Nationale d'Investissement, showed a consolidated net profit of up to 30 percent in 1996 compared with the previous year.
"But important stakes of the listed stocks results were non-recurrent elements...Therefore the 1997 profit growth will be lower compared with last year," Mouna Lahlou, a co-editor of CFI report said.

Some firms such as ONA subsidiaries Cosumar and Lesieur, the recently privatised Societe Cherifienne des Petroles and giant Samir oil firm SAMI.CS) benefited, at different levels, from subsidies of the state-owned Caisse de Compensation fund in 1996, a trade ministry official said.
"According to our first estimates for 1997, the listed stocks will show a drop in net profit to stabilise at an average 15 percent compared with the exceptional 30 percent in 1996," CFI said.
CFI forecasts around 900 million dirhams net profit for ONA, slightly up from 878.7 million dirhams in 1996 and 480 million dirhams for SNI in 1997 against 417 million dirhams last year.
ONA and SNI, which control diversified stakes in dozens of firms, are among the largest market capitalisation with 13.8 billion dirhams and 7.5 billion dirhams respectively.
Despite the bourse's gradual declining trend in the second quarter of 1997, stockbrokers do not expect a major drop in overall market activity.

"Operators on the bourse, such as mutual funds and insurance firms, are aware of speculation risks and artificial price rises...Therefore, it is expected the operators (will) moderate their investments to allow the market to maintain its share value at a stable level," Douiri added.

The legal framework, the domestic nature of investors' base and tight stock exchange rules remain a shield against any dramatic market drop or deflection of investments to a more attractive markets, officials said.
According to CFI, foreign investment, which represent an estimated five to six percent of total market capitalisation, remained unchanged since 1995.
Among the well-known investors are U.S. Morgan Stanley Asset Management and Salomon Brothers Assets Management and London-based Framlington fund.
Established in 1929, the Casablanca bourse has 47 listed stocks, a dozen stockbroker institutions and 30 active mutual funds.
